conventions.convention: States are indexed from zero; Qij is the rate from source j to destination i. Probability vectors are columns, off-diagonal generator entries are nonnegative, and generator columns sum to zero. A finite generator has at least one state.

The countable chain is given, time homogeneous, and nonexplosive, with finite total exit rate at each state. Nonnegative countable sums mean suprema of finite subsums. No existence or nonexplosion theorem for arbitrary countable rate matrices is asserted.

The finite projection set is nonempty. Killing occurs at the first exit, including time zero for initial states outside the set; later returns remain at the absorbing cemetery state. Initial cemetery mass includes all initial mass outside the set.
The countable-state distance is the full sum of absolute mass differences, without the factor one-half used in a total-variation convention.
The observable at the cemetery state is the midpoint of its supremum and infimum on S; the resulting observable bound has coefficient one-half times its oscillation.
The Poisson tail is P(N>K), with integer K≥0; the positive-parameter geometric bound requires μ<K+2, and parameter zero is treated separately.

For positive νt, time splitting uses m=ceil(νt) and μ=νt/m. Rounded execution requires validated scalar decisions and a separate vector-error certificate; missing certificates produce an explicit unavailable status.
Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are assumed in the immigration-death example only for the reaction-network construction and nonexplosion supplier.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite column generator Q and column probability vector p0, the unique differentiable solution of p′=Qp, p(0)=p0, is p(t)=exp(tQ)p0. For an admissible positive ν and P=I+Q/ν, p(t) is the Poisson-weighted mixture of P^k p0. If the admissible ν is zero, Q=0 and p(t)=p0.

For the given nonexplosive countable chain and finite nonempty F, the killed mass is P(Xt=x, τF>t), the cemetery mass is P(τF≤t), and the embedded killed-vector l1 error equals that cemetery mass. With the midpoint cemetery extension, bounded-observable error is at most half the oscillation times cemetery mass. The lifted law is exp(t Q̃F) times its initial law.

The exact one-series truncation has l1 error equal to its omitted Poisson mass. For positive νt, the split truncation Rμ,K^m p0 has exact transient l1 error 1−(sum from k=0 to K of exp(−μ)μ^k/k!)^m ≤ mτK(μ) ≤ mGK(μ). A separately certified arithmetic error adds by the triangle inequality.

For a finite real square matrix A, its factorial exponential series converges absolutely and uniformly on bounded time intervals, has derivative A exp(tA)=exp(tA)A and initial value I, and satisfies exp(A)exp(B)=exp(A+B) for commuting finite square matrices.
If Q is a finite column generator and ν dominates every exit rate, then for ν>0, P=I+Q/ν is nonnegative with every column sum one; if ν=0, Q=0.
For μ>0, integer K≥0, and μ<K+2, P(Pois(μ)>K) ≤ exp(−μ)μ^(K+1)/((K+1)!(1−μ/(K+2))). At μ=0 the tail is zero.

concerns.concern: The rounded Procedure says to 'set T to a validated upper bound for mG_K(μ)', but its final paragraph asserts 'the certified tail bound satisfies T≤ε'. The acceptance test bounds G_K(μ), not every subsequently chosen upper bound T. For example, take Q=0 on one state, admissible ν=1, t=1, ε=1, and B=1. Then m=1, μ=1, K=0, and G_0(1)=2/e<1, so the candidate passes. A backend returning T=2 supplies a valid outward upper bound for mG_0(1) and meets the stated backend conditions, yet violates T≤ε. The total error certificate remains valid, but the advertised tail-budget guarantee is unsupported for the rounded procedure as written.

seams_checked.note: The sparse page and actual matrix-free interface were inspected. Batch 47 uses operator applications without importing CSR representation, storage, operation-count, or finite-precision claims. The declared sparse-page prerequisite is contextual.

The prerequisite page concerns local defects and one-step stability. No such estimate is cited or used in the batch's exact matrix-exponential and Poisson-truncation arguments; this is a contextual page edge.

The reaction definition and complete Lyapunov nonexplosion theorem were checked against the immigration-death example. Its two channels have admissible poststates, finite rate 1+n, proper V(n)=1+n, and QV=1−n≤V. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are explicitly assumed. Other projection results assume a given nonexplosive chain.

The prerequisite page's compact-tube, stability, local-defect, and separate quadrature qualifications are not imported or weakened. Batch 47 makes no global ODE discretization or density-error claim; this is a contextual page edge.

The downstream page and cor-uniformized-generator-stationary-residual-certificate preserve the column convention and require positive admissible ν. Its F1–F3 faithfully state the generator, stochastic uniformization, and master-equation interfaces. The residual identity Qx/ν=Px−x and stationary-law identification use those interfaces correctly.

The downstream page and its item references were inspected. No listed item currently cites a batch-47 supplier. The source-factored algorithm independently defines its conservative column matrix and uses its own inverse lemma; no uniformization or transient-error proposition is restated.
